markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Qualitative feedback favors recent activity and repeated narrow interests. This motivates testing recency weighting, but does not establish that every category benefits. (2) Existing embedding and training-margin probes cannot establish generalization. A diagnostic change must ultimately improve the pinned validation HR@10. (3) Compatibility and purchase need are partially observed. Missing equipment information must remain unknown rather than become a negative label.

**Related work.** (1) [Sequence audits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) motivate comparisons with perturbed histories. [Availability-aware analyses](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) warn that order effects need not identify personal intent. (2) [Sampling reliability research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) motivates retaining identical validation candidates across comparisons. Diagnostic rankings cannot replace the benchmark objective. (3) [TREC product relations](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html) distinguish compatibility from association. These distinctions support evidence-based audits, but product relationships alone do not establish individual demand.

### Directions and framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal relevance | Recent versus older history | Recent-history residual | Sensitivity is not usefulness |
| Reliable diagnosis | Paired rankings and hits | Controlled perturbations | Training probes are descriptive |
| Practical suitability | Explicit title/description spans | Conflict-only pair audits | Unknown ownership and need |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / potential / implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder.

1. **Gated recent-history residual: 4/7/3.** Originality: useful combination, although pooling and gating are established. Potential: directly tests the reported temporal failure, although recent purchases may already satisfy demand. Difficulty: a small scoring addition, although predictor serialization must change.
2. **Matched temporal perturbation probe: 4/6/3.** Originality: controls improve existing audits, although perturbation methods are established. Potential: reusable architecture diagnostics, although sensitivity alone cannot improve ranking. Difficulty: uses existing hooks, although padding and paired sampling require care.
3. **Explicit-conflict pair audit: 5/6/6.** Originality: connects product-relation evidence to model diagnosis, although compatibility audits already exist. Potential: addresses practical mismatch, although coverage may be sparse. Difficulty: simple pair scoring, although reliable evidence extraction is substantial.

### Selected idea: gated recent-history residual

At 0% progress, prioritize idea 1 as a small, testable intervention. Preserve SASRec’s sequence representation and add a gated residual from the last five nonpadding item embeddings. This provides a direct route for recent evidence while retaining learned sequential features. Initialize the residual near zero and keep the baseline loss and optimizer for an interpretable comparison.

Train one baseline and one intervention with the specified seeds and epoch setting. Select solely by unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Use matched recent/old masking as descriptive evidence; preserve padding and report denominators. Compare paired validation hits and report uncertainty without claiming seed robustness or causal intent recovery.

Keep dataset routing and preprocessing unchanged. Save all artifacts beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer with the residual architecture. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe` and its compatibility hooks; use the actual scoring representation in margin probes and restore model mode afterward.

idea.description: Add a learnable gated residual from recent item embeddings to each SASRec sequence representation, with matching training, inference, and diagnostic scoring.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests insufficient emphasis on recent, specific interests. A small residual provides a controlled test of this hypothesis without introducing unsupported compatibility or purchase-need labels.
idea.implementation_notes: Use DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Preserve all four category models, routing, input splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior, defaulting to 200. At every training position, pool at most five nonpadding embeddings from the causal prefix; never include future positions. Normalize the pooled vector, gate it with a scalar sigmoid initialized near zero, and add it to the existing SASRec feature. Preserve the baseline loss and optimizer initially. Save the gate, normalization parameters, and window size in each category checkpoint. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py constructs the identical model and uses the final valid position. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Ensure log2feats exposes the augmented representation and predict_score uses the trained scoring function. Restore the model's previous training mode after probes. Category metadata breakdowns remain empty where unavailable; review data and simulator traits must not be fabricated. No improvement is established until independently evaluated.
idea.pseudocode:
class RecentResidualSASRec(SASRec):
    initialize gate_logit = -4.0
    initialize recent_norm = LayerNorm(hidden_dim)

    log2feats(sequence):
        base = original_sasrec_log2feats(sequence)
        embeddings = item_emb(sequence)
        recent = causal_mean_last_k_nonpadding(embeddings, sequence, k=5)
        augmented = base + sigmoid(gate_logit) * recent_norm(recent)
        return augmented * nonpadding_mask(sequence)

    # Keep the original item scoring and training objective.

train baseline and intervention using unchanged splits and specified seeds
write category checkpoints and matching working/predict.py
obtain host validation HR@10 for each category
select using the equal-weight mean of four category HR@10 values

DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis(loader):
    remember actual model training mode
    switch actual model to evaluation mode
    compute existing embedding and augmented-feature margin diagnostics
    optionally compare matched recent-item and old-item masking
    return metrics and explicit metric_definitions
    finally restore previous model mode

originality.positive: Combines a minimal temporal intervention with architecture-consistent diagnostics and a controlled benchmark comparison.
originality.negative: Recent-item pooling, residual connections, and scalar gates are established techniques; methodological novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: Provides a feasible foundation for testing when recent evidence improves recommendations across distinct categories.
future_potential.negative: Recency may amplify redundant purchases, and gains on sampled validation candidates may not transfer to broader recommendation quality.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small feature transformation and preserves the baseline objective and item-scoring interface.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal pooling, checkpoint compatibility, and predictor-writer parity require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: Uses shuffled-history comparisons to examine sequential structure across recommendation datasets.
limitations: Dataset-level perturbation results do not directly establish what a particular frozen encoder uses or whether recency weighting improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes arbitrary history shuffling from controls respecting item first-appearance times.
limitations: Observed order sensitivity can reflect item availability rather than individual intent.

related_work.title: RecSys 2025 sampling-reliability study
contributions: Examines how candidate sampling can change model rankings.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator or replacing its selection objective.

related_work.title: TREC 2025 Product Recommendation task definitions
contributions: Separates substitutes, complements, unknown compatibility, explicit incompatibility, and insufficient evidence.
limitations: Product-pair relationships do not establish ownership, replacement need, or individual purchase intent.
